newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S PLANNERS QUERY IOC REFINERY.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S PLANNERS QUERY IOC REFINERY.

text.p: India's Planning Commission has called into question key elements of Indian Oil Corp's plan to build a nine million tonne refinery in the eastern state of Orissa, a government official said on Friday.

The commission, the government agency which sets public spending priorities, has questioned the proposed site and target date, as well as IOC's decision to increase the refinery's capacity to nine million tonnes from six million, he said.
The state-run IOC proposes to commission the refinery at Abhayachanderpur in 2001/02 (April-March).
But the Planning Commission believes the nation's supply and demand situation will not justify the refinery until 2006/07 -- five years later, the official in the Petroleum Ministry said.

"Based on demand-supply projections, the Planning Commission has said the refinery would be required in 2006/07 and not 2001/02 as indicated by IOC," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters.
A committee within the Petroleum Ministry has forecast a product surplus until 2005/06, with a marginal deficit of 1.93 million tonnes in 2006/07, he said.
But a member of IOC's board of directors said the supply-demand projections were being reviewed.
"There is a possibility of a deficit situation emerging in 2001/02, which will establish the need for the East Coast refinery," the IOC director said.
The commission is also opposed to the location of the refinery in the eastern region which could have product surplus of at least 6.7 million tonnes beginning in 2001/02.
"This may create problems of evacuating the products to a deficit region," the Petroleum Ministry offical said.
The commission has also questioned IOC's decision to increase the capacity of the proposed refinery to nine million tonne from the approved six million.
The ministry official said the commission believes IOC needs to seek fresh approval from the Public Investment Board.
The IOC director said the issues were being considered by IOC, and an explanation would soon be submitted to the commission.
The refinery is proposed to be set up by a joint venture of IOC and Kuwait Petroleum Corp, each of which will hold 26 percent stakes.
